stem_block:
Questions 1-4 refer to Passage A15 - Teaching a Plant to Defend Itself Faster

The molecule at the centre of this work, (1) ........ , is made naturally by many plants and is given off in larger amounts by damaged tissue. It was already known that treated plants became less attractive to certain insects, but nobody had settled whether the substance builds defences outright or merely leaves them ready to be built. To find out, young maize seedlings were sprayed with a weak water-based emulsion of it while their controls received the wetting agent alone, and both lots then stood in a warm glasshouse for a full day before the infestation began. Each seedling was afterwards sealed in a chamber so that whatever its leaves released could be caught and identified. Over the first six hours the treated plants gave off more of two sesquiterpenes than untreated plants that were equally infested, and in parallel choice tests (2) ........ offered two streams of air settled more often on the one coming from untreated plants. By (3) ........ hours, though, the two groups could no longer be told apart. A second run dispensed with insects altogether: leaves were lightly scratched and painted with jasmonic acid at (4) ........ to imitate an attack, and the treated plants again reacted harder on the first day. The team regards the brevity of the advantage as exactly what preparation, rather than outright activation, would predict.

Questions 5-8 refer to Passage A19 - Turning Salt Water into Drinking Water with Sunlight

Once the still had been assembled the team simply watched it work, taking a reading every hour from 08:00 until (5) ........ and measuring what each hour had produced. The best conditions proved to be both sets of mirrors in use with the water only two centimetres deep. Taking the outside mirror away cost more than extra depth did: the shallow version dropped to 7.84 litres a day, while the deeper one sank to (6) ........ litres, the weakest of the four trials. On the stricter exergy scale, which asks how much genuinely useful work the sunlight performed, even the best run scored only (7) ........ per cent, far below its score on the plain energy measure and a reminder that most of what is captured leaves as low-grade heat rather than as fresh water. The whole exercise was the work of a team at an engineering university in (8) ........ , who had taken a plain still of a familiar design apart and rebuilt it piece by piece to find out what each change was worth.

Questions 9-15 refer to Passage G07 - What Houseplants Really Do to the Air Indoors

The first of three studies borrowed three closely matched offices in a well-insulated Australian building and measured each of them empty, lightly planted and heavily planted, with the air conditioning switched off and the sensors placed (9) ........ metres above the floor, roughly where a seated worker breathes. Only dampness responded. With no plants at all the median relative humidity sat at 29.1 per cent, dry enough to leave eyes and throats uncomfortable, while the fullest arrangement of ferns lifted it to (10) ........ per cent, still well short of the point at which mould starts to be a worry. Neither the temperature of the rooms nor their carbon dioxide moved at all.

The second study shut a single plant at a time inside a sealed cube and pumped particles through it at three strengths, the weakest around 800 and the strongest about (11) ........ per cubic centimetre. Leaf surfaces mattered more than expected: the species that trapped most was the (12) ........ , whose leaves carry deep grooves and fine hairs on both faces, whereas the smoothest and least hairy leaves in the set trapped least. Rinsing the leaves made the gap visible in another way, since a square centimetre of the best collector held 5.286 micrograms of sulphate against (13) ........ micrograms on the same area of the worst. The awkward finding came when ordinary outdoor air was used in place of a prepared mist, for the chambers then no longer reliably held less than the empty control: at eight in the morning the honey locust's chamber held more, and by six in the evening so did the (14) ........ . A bushy plant, the researchers suspect, slows the air enough for particles to linger rather than pass through.

The third study asked about people rather than air. (15) ........ office workers each sat for five minutes in a bare room, in a room planted in a Japanese style and in a room of tropical species before taking attention tests. The Japanese room left them less negatively disposed than either of the others, though no arrangement lifted positive feeling and none changed how accurately or how quickly they worked.

yeniden_uretim.yol_gerekcesi: Kutu (word_bank) kurulmadi. Listeden secmeli alt tur olcumde %71 sizinti verdi; kutu korunacaksa adaylarin en az ikisinin cerceveye oturmasi gerekiyordu. Bu paketteki her bosluk metnin KENDI sectigi bir ada/sayiya aciliyor, dolayisiyla kutu kurmak adaylarin tamamini disaridan gorulebilir kilardi (bir sayi listesi verildiginde aday buyukluk sirasindan cikarim yapar). Kelime-yazmali yol hem receteye uygun hem de bu bosluklarda daha dayanikli.
yeniden_uretim.bosluk_gerekcesi: Katilimci sayisi calismanin kendi degeri; ozetin baska hicbir yerinde bir sayi tekrarlanmiyor (onceki ozette gecen saksi sayisi bilerek yaziya dokulmedi) ki bosluk yankiyla doldurulmasin.
